title: Rafael and the Signal
premise: Wren Zhou, an investigator of impossible accidents on the forgotten colony of Meridian's Reach, discovers the nine-second gravity flicker was a distress pulse from the relay at the edge of dead space — a signal the colonial authority intends to silence rather than answer, because answering means admitting the colony was never meant to survive. As she races across the dying system with a disgraced pilot named Rafael, whose name she took from a dead man's manifest, she uncovers that she herself is a memory-wiped witness to the original cover-up. At the relay, she must choose between transmitting the truth that will save the remaining colonists and destroy her own identity, or staying invisible and letting the signal — and the colony — die.
about_author: Freya Galloway is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction about people who investigate the unexplainable. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. During a routine inspection of a collapsed habitat dome, gravity flickers system-wide for exactly nine seconds, killing three workers. Wren, who investigates impossible accidents, notices her instruments recorded the flicker before it happened. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Wren reviews a decade of 'impossible accidents' on Meridian's Reach and finds a pattern: every incident clusters along a line pointing toward the dead-space relay. POV shifts briefly to a dying archivist who begs her to forget what she's found. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being the only one who sees.

chapters.title: A Name from a Manifest
chapters.summary: Wren seeks out Rafael Okonkwo, a disgraced freight pilot blacklisted for claiming he once received a transmission from the relay. But the real Rafael died years ago; the man using his identity is a deserter named Tomas. POV: Wren, then Tomas. Emotional beat: two people built from false papers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Authority Knows
chapters.summary: Colonial administrator Ilsa Voss summons Wren, offers a promotion, and warns her off the flicker investigation with unsettling precision. Wren realizes Voss knows about the pattern. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the chill of realizing invisibility is a service she provides to someone.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Wren and Tomas steal a decommissioned survey ship and burn for the outer system, pursued by authority patrol craft. In transit, Tomas confesses he heard the relay signal: a voice counting down. POV: alternating Wren and Tomas. Emotional beat: trust kindling in the dark.

chapters.title: Ghost in Her Own File
chapters.summary: Wren decrypts her own sealed personnel record and finds gaps: eleven missing years, a redacted birthplace, a medical file for a woman with her face but another name. Emotional beat: vertigo — she has been investigating her own disappearance all along.

chapters.title: The Colony That Was Never Promised
chapters.summary: Flashback chapters within Wren's surfacing memories reveal Meridian's Reach was an actuarial experiment: a colony the parent corporation insured against itself, designed to fail profitably. POV: Wren's recovered memories. Emotional beat: grief for a self she can't fully reclaim.

chapters.title: Voss's Mercy
chapters.summary: Ilsa Voss's POV. She was the young administrator who signed the first cover-up and has spent twenty years protecting colonists from a truth she believes would cause mass despair and violence. Emotional beat: a villain who thinks she is a savior.

chapters.title: Ambush at Cinder Drift
chapters.summary: Patrol craft corner Wren and Tomas at a derelict mining station. They escape by venting the station's atmosphere behind them, killing two patrol pilots. Tomas breaks; Wren stays cold and functional. Emotional beat: the first price of survival, paid in someone else's blood.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Static
chapters.summary: As they cross into dead space, the ship's receivers pick up the relay signal directly: a woman's voice reciting names — including Wren's original name. Emotional beat: terror and longing braided together; the past is calling her by name.

chapters.title: What Rafael Knew
chapters.summary: Tomas reveals the real Rafael Okonkwo was a relay technician who discovered the countdown and died transmitting it — the signal is his, still looping, still waiting for someone to finish it. Emotional beat: Tomas's guilt transmuted into purpose; Wren inherits a stranger's mission.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Abandonment
chapters.summary: Wren works the numbers: the flicker was the relay's dying gravity anchor, and in nineteen days the relay's core breaches, taking the colony's comm and navigation grid with it. Every ship in system will go blind. Emotional beat: cold clarity — this is an accident she can actually prevent.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Voss's flagship intercepts them at the system's edge. Voss offers Wren her missing years — the full record, her original identity — in exchange for turning back. Emotional beat: temptation as a knife; the offer is everything she's been searching for.

chapters.title: The Woman She Was
chapters.summary: Wren takes the files and reads them alone: she was the relay's chief engineer, the one who designed the cover-up's technical architecture, who wiped her own memory to become an unimpeachable witness. Emotional beat: self-horror — she built the prison she's been escaping.

chapters.title: Tomas's Choice
chapters.summary: Tomas learns his blacklisting was engineered to place a deniable pilot near the relay; his entire outlaw life was someone's contingency. He nearly walks away, then chooses to stay. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: choosing love and duty when both are built on lies.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: They reach the relay: a cathedral of dead machinery still humming with Rafael Okonkwo's loop. The countdown is at four days. Voss's ships hold position, weapons hot, waiting. Emotional beat: awe curdled with siege-panic.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Inside the relay, Wren finds her own old engineering logs and the manual override — and understands the gravity flicker was her own fail-safe, triggered by her past self, a message she left for the woman she would become. Emotional beat: reconciliation across the wound of her own amnesia.

chapters.title: The Transmission
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren begins broadcasting the full truth to every colony channel. Voss fires on the relay; Tomas flies the survey ship into the firing line, buying seconds with his hull. Wren completes the transmission as the relay's core breaches. Emotional beat: sacrifice, defiance, and the terrible relief of finally being seen.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: The truth reaches the colonies: corporations begin evacuating Meridian's Reach under public pressure. Voss, exposed, chooses not to fire on the escape pods — her last mercy is real. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: a savior-complex dismantled by the people she tried to protect.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: Wren, injured and half-deaf from the breach, is pulled from the debris by rescue crews who know her name — both names. The colonists begin organizing their own exodus, no longer waiting to be saved or silenced. Emotional beat: battered, hard-won hope.

chapters.title: The Price, Itemized
chapters.summary: Wren testifies before the inquiry, refusing to let her amnesia excuse her past complicity. Tomas, gravely wounded but alive, waits for her outside. Emotional beat: accountability as an act of love — she chooses to carry what she did.

chapters.title: Rafael and the Signal
chapters.summary: Final chapter. Wren takes the name Rafael Okonkwo for her new identity — not erasing him, but finishing his transmission by living it. The last scene mirrors the first: nine seconds of silence, this time chosen, as she and Tomas watch the colony ships burn for open space. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity self-made, love chosen over duty's ashes.
